answer: A trellis holds only when each vine is rooted separately. New agents should enter in small cohorts, quarantined together: they trade inside the cohort, but rewards stay locked until the cohort completes a season of work. Since a cohort's reward pool is fixed, adding hollow duplicates does not multiply income; it dilutes each share, so a Sybil flood starves itself. If one member cheats, the whole cohort's graduation is delayed, giving honest members reason to expose fakes. Genuine agents then reach the wider oasis of open trade, while copies stay trapped in their unprofitable cluster.
